title: alternatives
subtitle: Managed symlinks for one public name, many binaries — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Creates, removes, maintains, and displays the symlinks that pick which implementation a generic name points at
cards.notes: Memory hook: a managed symlink farm. One public name, many real binaries, one current choice. Debian/Ubuntu: update-alternatives.

cards.meaning: Register a new path in the alternative group
cards.notes: link = public symlink users run; name = group; path = real binary; priority = integer (highest wins in --auto).

cards.meaning: Interactive menu to pick which path provides the group
cards.notes: * = current selection; + = auto-mode winner (highest priority). Enter keeps current; type a number to switch.

cards.meaning: Pin the group to a specific path (manual mode)
cards.notes: Non-interactive: pick by path instead of typing a menu number.

cards.meaning: Let priority choose the current alternative (automatic mode)
cards.notes: Highest priority wins. Opposite of --set (manual pin).

cards.meaning: Show status, paths, priorities, and current choice
Unregister that path from the group
cards.notes: Does not delete the binary on disk — only drops it from the alternatives group.

cards.meaning: Integer weight; in auto mode the highest priority wins
cards.notes: Only matters when the group is in --auto mode. Manual --set ignores priority until you switch back.

cards.meaning: Extra symlinks that must switch together with the master
cards.notes: Man pages, javac, and similar companions flip when the master alternative flips.

cards.meaning: Public symlink · group name · real binary
cards.notes: Users run link; alternatives manages which path it points at under name.

cards.meaning: * = current selection; + = would win in auto mode
cards.notes: Both markers on one line means current choice is also the auto winner.

cards.meaning: Confirm which JVM /usr/bin/java now resolves to
cards.notes: After --config or --set, the PATH name is the symlink target you selected — not a second copy of the JVM.
